context_only: # tp v0.34.0 — Trustworthy writes, and less of everything else

tasks.title: Derive the guard-test list
tasks.acceptance:
- spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md lists every test function added between the v0.32.0 and v0.33.0 tags under the `## Guard tests` heading, one file:function per line, with the placeholder declaration line deleted
- The derivation passes --no-ext-diff and an empty result is treated as a failed derivation rather than a result
- python3 scripts/check-measured-claims.py exits 0 with no PENDING line

tasks.title: Lock the import write path
tasks.acceptance:
- importcmd.go's read-modify-write runs inside engine.WithFileLock honouring the resolved lock_timeout_seconds
- A lock held past the timeout exits 4 carrying LockTimeoutError's hint with the lock path and elapsed wait
- The success path gains no flag and no output change

tasks.title: Lock the init write path
tasks.acceptance:
- init.go's stat-then-write runs inside engine.WithFileLock, including the path tp add --spec reaches through runInit
- tp init and tp add --spec each exit 4 with LockTimeoutError's hint when the lock is held past the timeout
- No unlocked task-file write remains in the tool

tasks.title: Make add --bulk honour the cap
tasks.acceptance:
- tp add --bulk adopts the shared 1MB line cap and aborts with exit 3 naming the file and line number
- An over-long row no longer discards itself and every row after it while reporting success
- The warn-and-continue tests asserting the removed behaviour move in this task
source_sections: ## 4. The bulk readers honour the shared line cap

tasks.title: Make set --bulk honour the cap
tasks.acceptance:
- tp set --bulk adopts the shared 1MB line cap and aborts with exit 3 naming the file and line number
- The task file is left byte-identical when the operation aborts
- The warn-and-continue tests asserting the removed behaviour move in this task
source_sections: ## 4. The bulk readers honour the shared line cap

tasks.title: Remove the line-cap exemption markers
tasks.acceptance:
- The `line-cap:` markers come out of add.go and set.go now that neither reader is exempt
- The guard enforcing the shared cap no longer lists either bulk reader as an exception
source_sections: ## 4. The bulk readers honour the shared line cap

tasks.title: Put -race in the project gate
tasks.acceptance:
- The project gate in .tp/config.json runs the whole test suite under -race before golangci-lint
- Any data race the new gate surfaces is fixed in this task, since the gate runs at its own close
- skills/tp/SKILL.md recommends -race for any Go project using tp
source_sections: ## 5. The quality gate sees data races

tasks.title: Remove the masking gate overrides
tasks.acceptance:
- The gate resolved for this release's task file runs -race
- A config guard test compares the resolved value against the literal gate string rather than against the project value
- That test fails when the project gate weakens and when an override is reintroduced
source_sections: ## 5. The quality gate sees data races

tasks.title: Drop the flag from init recipes
tasks.acceptance:
- CLAUDE.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md no longer instruct tp init --quality-gate, so a later cycle does not re-create the override
- Only the recipes change; section 8.3 governs where the flag stays documented
source_sections: ## 5. The quality gate sees data races

tasks.title: Enable dupl at its default threshold
tasks.acceptance:
- dupl is enabled in .golangci.yml over production and test files alike at its own default threshold, which is not raised
- Every clone it reports is merged, or exempted with its reason recorded at the site when merging would need a new abstraction
- golangci-lint run is clean with dupl enabled at this task's close

tasks.title: Inline single-caller indirection
tasks.acceptance:
- Helpers with one call site, interfaces with one implementation, and parameters every caller passes the same value for are inlined
- Indirection is kept only where a second caller exists today and can be named
- Each removal names in its evidence that it had no caller or the implementation that absorbed it

tasks.title: Remove unreachable branches
tasks.acceptance:
- Error branches for states the type system excludes and default arms after an exhaustive switch are removed rather than tested
- Nil checks on values constructed non-nil in the same function are removed
- Each removal names what now covers it

- A guard surviving its own mutation unchanged is rewritten to assert what it claims, or removed with the surviving coverage named

tasks.title: Reduce same-path duplicate assertions
tasks.acceptance:
- Where several tests assert one property through the same path, the one whose failure message best identifies the defect is kept
- Tests asserting the same property through different paths all stay, because that is coverage rather than duplication

tasks.title: Unpin implementation-detail assertions
tasks.acceptance:
- Tests pinning an exact log string, a private helper's shape, or a map's iteration order are converted to assert the observable contract
- Those that cannot be converted are removed with the surviving coverage named

tasks.title: Give every fact one home
tasks.acceptance:
- README.md owns the install and command index, SKILL.md owns everything needed mid-cycle, CLAUDE.md owns this repository's conventions, REFERENCE.md owns exhaustive detail
- Anything duplicated across two homes is cut from the non-owner
- The command index and the command forms are the one permitted overlap

tasks.title: Qualify the register-a-check rule
tasks.acceptance:
- CLAUDE.md's instruction to register a mechanical check for a class seen in three rounds becomes conditional on the phase
- The qualifier states that a check registered before its subject exists suppresses a class for every reviewer while verifying only what already exists

tasks.title: Complete the lint rule table
tasks.acceptance:
- README.md's table lists every rule tp can emit, one line each
- A test fails when a rule tp can emit is undocumented, and the collected list's own blind spot is recorded beside it
- The assertion fails on today's tree before the table is completed
source_sections: ### 8.2 The lint rule table is complete and stays complete

tasks.title: Document the six missing flags
tasks.acceptance:
- --reason-file and --stdin on done and close, --docs-path, --test-path, --base on audit, --commit-strategy on init are added to the inventory in SKILL.md
- A test fails when the CLI registers an undocumented flag, and when the inventory documents a flag the CLI does not register
- The inventory records what exists rather than what to recommend

tasks.title: Exit 2 on an unknown command
tasks.acceptance:
- tp with an unknown command or subcommand exits 2, matching the documented scheme
- The assertion fails on today's tree, where an unknown command exits 1
source_sections: ### 9.1 An unknown command is a usage error

tasks.title: Name the right object in validation hints
tasks.acceptance:
- Validation errors from commands whose object is not the task file carry a hint naming their own object
- TestFileErrorsCarryAHint enumerates ExitValidation sites the way it enumerates ExitFile sites
- A new site cannot join the class without the enumeration failing
source_sections: ### 9.2 The validation hint channel stops handing out task-file advice

tasks.title: Give lint.go its spec hint
tasks.acceptance:
- tp lint emits specFileMissingHint on a missing spec and leaves taskFileCommands
- Every hintless ExitFile site in lint.go gains a hint in this task
- tp init is untouched because runInit never stats the spec
source_sections: ### 9.3 `lint` names the spec, not the task file

tasks.title: Recommend example tables in acceptance
tasks.acceptance:
- SKILL.md's decomposition guidance states input-to-expected-output tables as the recommended shape for behavioural acceptance
- It names the secondary benefit that a concrete expected value forces ambiguity out in the interview step
source_sections: ### 10.1 Example tables are the acceptance shape for behavioural tasks

tasks.title: Record what the release removed
tasks.acceptance:
- The release notes carry before-and-after counts for source lines, test count, exported symbols, documentation lines, and facts with more than one home
- They are recorded as fact rather than measured against a target, since discrimination and not line count is the metric
source_sections: ### 2.3 The release records what it removed

tasks.title: State the release's task kinds
tasks.acceptance:
- Each task in this release declares in its acceptance whether it is a removal or a repair
- A task that only adds cites the section of this spec that mandates the addition

tasks.title: Hold the release inside its non-goals
tasks.acceptance:
- No task adds a command or a flag, changes convergence policy, runs writing units in parallel, or edits a historical spec
- No removal requires designing a new abstraction to hold a merged form
